# Repositories

Each repository is served by its own adapter and described by a static profile in `config/repositories/`. A profile is code, not runtime configuration: changing what can be searched, filtered, or faceted means changing the profile and passing schema validation at startup.

| ID | Name | Holds | Platform | Canonical API | Record ID form |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jscholarship` | JScholarship | Institutional repository: theses, dissertations, articles, and reports. | DSpace 2024.1 | DSpace REST API | `jscholarship:<uuid>` |
| `jhrdr` | JHRDR | Johns Hopkins Research Data Repository: research datasets. | Dataverse 6.10.1 | Dataverse Native API | `jhrdr:<persistent-id>` |

## Search capabilities

A concept marked `no` is never translated into backend syntax. For filters, the response carries an `unsupported_filter` warning and the rest of the search runs. An unsupported search field or sort fails for that repository; an unsupported facet is skipped with a warning.

### Search fields (`field`)

| Field | JScholarship | JHRDR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keyword` | yes | yes |
| `title` | yes | yes |
| `creator` | yes | yes |
| `subject` | yes | yes |
| `abstract` | yes | yes |

### Filters (`filters.*`)

| Filter | JScholarship | JHRDR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dateFrom` | yes | yes |
| `dateTo` | yes | yes |
| `resourceTypes` | yes | no |
| `creators` | yes | no |
| `subjects` | yes | yes |
| `collections` | yes | yes |
| `access` | no | no |

### Sort options (`sort`)

| Sort | JScholarship | JHRDR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `relevance` | yes | yes |
| `date_asc` | yes | yes |
| `date_desc` | yes | yes |
| `title_asc` | yes | yes |

### Facets (`list_facets`)

| Facet | JScholarship | JHRDR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | yes | yes |

| `subject` | yes | yes |
| `year` | yes | yes |
| `resourceType` | yes | yes |
| `collection` | yes | yes |

## Public-access rules

Every Solr request from an adapter carries its profile's immutable public filters. No client input can remove, weaken, or negate them. They only narrow the candidate set; each returned record is still confirmed public through the canonical API (see [Canonical gate](../architecture/canonical-gate.md)).

### JScholarship

- Restrict to Item resource type only
- Only the latest version of each item
- Exclude withdrawn items
- Exclude non-discoverable items
- Only items readable by the anonymous group (DSpace 9 UUID)

### JHRDR

- Restrict to Dataset documents only (exclude Dataverse collections and DataFiles)
- Only datasets with a published version
- Exclude deaccessioned datasets (may co-occur with Published in multiValued field)

## Full-text search

| Repository | Enabled | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JScholarship | no | DSpace indexes bitstream content from all bundles into fulltext, including restricted/embargoed bitstreams on public items. The DSpace team disabled full-text highlighting for this reason (DS-3498). The MCP cannot use this field for search, ranking, facets, or any returned value until a Phase 0 proof demonstrates all indexed content is publicly accessible. |
| JHRDR | no | The \_text\_ catchall field contains copyField content from metadata fields only (not file content). However, it is kept out of the explicit keyword query field list because it uses text\_general (basic tokenization without stemming), and the specific metadata fields with text\_en analysis provide better relevance. The \_text\_ field may be enabled as a fallback in a future phase. |
